items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: I remember Bucky Pizzarelli talking about the chart on Ray Charles’ arrangement

ctx.x: Oh yeah. No one would know who was the ghost writer on a lot of these arrangements. They might have a big name out there, you know this is this person, this is this arranger. But the ghost writing that goes underneath would be much different.

Yes. I remember Bucky Pizzarelli talking about the chart on Ray Charles’ arrangement of “Georgia” and he said, “You know we’re still not sure who actually wrote it.” It’s got someone’s name but he could have farmed it out, it could have been farmed twice or — that’s the music business I guess.

I’ll tell you something too that a lot of people don’t know and wouldn’t know unless I told them, you know Hank Crawford, Hank Crawford had a style of making an eight piece group sound like a big band. He got that, he learned that from my teacher whose name is Mr. William W. Davis. We called him Prof. Davis. He came to Jackson State and he started with Prof. and Hank Crawford and I used to talk about that. Prof Davis was probably one of the best arrangers that I knew. He wrote for the marching band.
